jurisdiction.name: Holy See / Vatican City
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Vatican City State has one binding AI instrument: the Governorate's Decree No. DCCII setting guidelines on artificial intelligence, in force since 1 January 2025, which sets principles for AI use in the State and creates an AI Commission. Its 2024 data protection regulation provides the data protection baseline. Otherwise the Holy See steers AI mainly through papal and dicastery teaching, including the 2024 World Day of Peace message calling for a binding international AI treaty, the 2025 doctrinal note Antiqua et nova and the 2026 encyclical Magnifica humanitas, and in May 2026 it set up an Interdicasterial Commission on AI.
lead_institutions: Dicastery for the Doctrine of the Faith
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026 from the Vatican City State legislation listings and the Holy See's official websites. Not yet verified from the official text: individual issues of the Acta Apostolicae Sedis and material from the financial supervisor. The implementing rules the AI decree calls for and the guidelines the new AI commission is preparing are tracked as leads.

instruments.current_status: Dated 28 January 2025 ('Dato in Roma ... il 28 gennaio 2025') and approved by the Supreme Pontiff at the audience of 14 January 2025, who ordered its publication; the official English version is on vatican.va. Magisterial guidance; no binding legal effect in Vatican City State law.
instruments.summary: Doctrinal note of two Holy See dicasteries, approved by Pope Francis at an audience on 14 January 2025, setting out the Church's position on AI compared with human intelligence. It addresses AI's use and ethical implications in society, work, health care, education, misinformation and deepfakes, privacy and surveillance, the environment and warfare (including autonomous weapons), and stresses that moral responsibility for AI's use always rests with humans. It is addressed to those engaged in education and the transmission of the faith and to all concerned with technological progress.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Holy See's main doctrinal statement on AI ethics; frames the guidelines and the 2026 encyclical.

instruments.official_title: N. DCCII – Decreto della Pontificia Commissione per lo Stato della Città del Vaticano recante “Linee Guida in materia di intelligenza artificiale”
instruments.english_title: Decree No. DCCII of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State on the Guidelines on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State
instruments.current_status: In force since 1 January 2025 (art. 2 of the decree: 'entra in vigore il 1° gennaio duemilaventicinque'); signed 16 December 2024 by Card. Fernando Vérgez Alzaga as President. Art. 15 of the annex required implementing laws and regulations within twelve months of entry into force and art. 13 announced a separate implementing regulation on AI in security and cybersecurity; neither appeared in the Governorate's official legislation listings as of 12 October 2026 (see leads). The decree states it is also to be published in the AAS supplement.
instruments.summary: Decree promulgating 15-article AI guidelines that bind the Governorate of Vatican City State, its operational and scientific bodies, the Vatican judicial organs, Governorate staff and public-contract suppliers. It bans seven AI practices (including discriminatory anthropological inferences, subliminal manipulation, excluding persons with disabilities and uses threatening State security), requires AI-generated content to be labelled 'IA', keeps decisions with humans in administration, health and justice (AI in the courts only for organising work and legal research) and requires a regulatory impact analysis before AI is used in administrative procedures. It creates a five-member Commission on Artificial Intelligence chaired by the Secretary General to draft implementing laws, give opinions on AI deployments and report every six months.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Vatican City State's only binding AI-specific instrument; sets prohibited practices, sector principles and the AI Commission.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 8-page decree and annex PDF read (pdftotext) from the Governorate's 'Normativa generale' listing on vaticanstate.va; dates from the decree itself

instruments.official_title: N. DCLVII – Decreto della Pontificia Commissione per lo Stato della Città del Vaticano con il quale viene promulgato il Regolamento Generale sulla protezione dei Dati personali
instruments.english_title: Decree No. DCLVII of the Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State promulgating the General Regulation on the Protection of Personal Data
instruments.issuing_authority: Pontifical Commission for Vatican City State
instruments.current_status: In force since 30 April 2024 (art. 3 of the decree; art. 28 of the Regulation: in force immediately, ad experimentum for three years), so the experimental period runs to about April 2027. Referenced by Decree No. DCCII (AI guidelines) arts. 5 and 11.
instruments.summary: Decree promulgating, ad experimentum for three years, a 28-article General Regulation on personal data protection for the Governorate of Vatican City State. It sets processing principles, lawful bases, special-category rules, records of processing, a Data Protection Officer (RPD) and data-subject rights including access, erasure, portability, objection (including to profiling for direct marketing) and restriction. Privacy notices must disclose the existence of automated decision-making; complaints go to the RPD, with a final reasoned order by the President of the Governorate.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General data protection law that the AI guidelines (Decree No. DCCII, arts. 5 and 11) require all AI data processing to follow.
instruments.evidence_reference: curl (browser user agent, --max-time 60): full 20-page PDF read (pdftotext) from the Governorate's 'Normativa generale' listing on vaticanstate.va; dates from the decree itself

instruments.official_title: Lettera Enciclica Magnifica humanitas del Santo Padre Leone XIV sulla custodia della persona umana nel tempo dell'intelligenza artificiale
instruments.english_title: Encyclical Letter Magnifica humanitas of Pope Leo XIV on Safeguarding the Human Person in the Time of Artificial Intelligence
instruments.current_status: Signed 15 May 2026 ('Dato a Roma, presso San Pietro, il 15 maggio dell'anno 2026'); papal magisterial teaching, not a legal norm of Vatican City State, with the official English version on vatican.va. Some outside sources report public release on 25 May 2026; the record uses the date stated in the document.
instruments.summary: First encyclical of Pope Leo XIV, applying Catholic social doctrine to artificial intelligence in five chapters. Chapter three treats AI as a valuable tool requiring vigilance and sets out expectations on responsibility, transparency and the governance of AI; chapter four covers truth and democracy, education, work and dependencies in the digital transition; chapter five addresses weapons and AI and calls for multilateral diplomacy. It is addressed to the Church and to all people of good will and steers the Holy See's AI policy positions.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Highest-level Holy See statement on AI governance and ethics (papal magisterium).

instruments.official_title: Messaggio di Sua Santità Francesco per la LVII Giornata Mondiale della Pace. Intelligenza artificiale e pace
instruments.english_title: Message of Pope Francis for the 57th World Day of Peace (1 January 2024): Artificial Intelligence and Peace
instruments.current_status: Dated 8 December 2023 ('Dal Vaticano, 8 dicembre 2023') for the World Day of Peace on 1 January 2024; a policy statement, not a treaty or legal norm. The 'international' category reflects its call for a binding international AI treaty, not a signature or ratification.
instruments.summary: Papal message for the World Day of Peace of 1 January 2024 devoted to AI, addressed to nations, heads of State and Government and civil society. It sets ethical expectations for AI development (human dignity, transparency, non-discrimination, accountability), warns about autonomous weapon systems, and urges the community of nations to adopt a binding international treaty regulating the development and use of AI.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: States the Holy See's diplomatic position calling for a binding international AI treaty.

instruments.official_title: Rescriptum ex Audientia SS.mi circa l'istituzione della Commissione Interdicasteriale sull'Intelligenza Artificiale
instruments.english_title: Rescript ex Audientia on the establishment of the Interdicasterial Commission on Artificial Intelligence
instruments.issuing_authority: Dicastery for Promoting Integral Human Development (Prefect), with the approval of Pope Leo XIV
instruments.current_status: Rescript signed 12 May 2026 ('Dal Vaticano, 12 maggio 2026') by Cardinal Michael Czerny and published in Holy See Press Office Bulletin No. 0416 of 16 May 2026; the effective date is taken as the signature date, as the rescript states no separate commencement clause. The Dicastery reports the commission's first meeting on 17 June 2026; no Holy See AI-use guidelines from it were published by 12 October 2026.
instruments.summary: Rescript recording Pope Leo XIV's approval (audience of 3 May 2026) of an Interdicasterial Commission on Artificial Intelligence, set up under art. 28 §5 of Praedicate Evangelium. The commission brings together the Dicasteries for Integral Human Development, Doctrine of the Faith, Culture and Education and Communication and the Pontifical Academies for Life, Sciences and Social Sciences, each represented by a delegate. Coordination rests with the Dicastery for Integral Human Development for a renewable year, and the coordinator facilitates information exchange on AI activities and projects, including policies on AI use within the Holy See.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Founding instrument of the Holy See's cross-curial AI coordination body, which is to develop internal AI-use policies.

Coverage note (original): Technical review notes: tier B/C batch run 2026-10-12, one agent, national level only (PROTOCOL §6), about 25-minute time box. vaticanstate.va 'Legislazione e normativa' (5 listings) scanned; DCCII and DCLVII read in full; Fundamental Law 31 Jul 2026: no AI. AAS not searched issue by issue; ASIF by web search only. Antiqua et nova (i-40bc474c2d90) re-identified to Italian original; domain-named org o-2aa2c336ebea pruned. Magisterial documents recorded nonbinding_guidance; rescript administrative_policy_mandatory_in_scope. World Day of Peace 2024 message: 'international' category removed at merge (calls for a treaty; no treaty signed). Titles 'N. DCCII –'/'N. DCLVII –' follow official headers (validator warns). Rome Call (romecall.org) fails third-party-host rule - lead. Convention 108: not a party. Units covered: Law: Governorate legislation portal (vaticanstate.va 'Legislazione e normativa': all five listings scanned; AI decree DCCII and data protection decree DCLVII read in full; new Fundamental Law of 31 July 2026 searched, no AI provisions). No AI implementing laws (art. 15 DCCII) found. Acta Apostolicae Sedis not searched issue-by-issue; AAS is cited in the documents but the vaticanstate.va listing is the State's official publication channel.; Government: Holy See: Supreme Pontiff (encyclical Magnifica humanitas, World Day of Peace 2024 message), DDF / Dicastery for Culture and Education (Antiqua et nova), Dicastery for Integral Human Development (Interdicasterial Commission rescript, Press Office Bulletin 0416). No national AI strategy exists: searched, nothing found.; Ministries: Dicasteries' own AI documents: DDF and Culture and Education (Antiqua et nova); Integral Human Development (commission); Pontifical Academy for Life (Rome Call, lead only). Governorate Directorates (health, museums, infrastructure, telecoms, security) have AI principles only inside DCCII; no separate directorate AI documents found.; Regulators: Data protection: Governorate RPD under DCLVII, no AI guidance found. Financial supervisor ASIF: searched, no AI-specific documents. No telecom/media, competition or cyber regulator with AI documents found (DCCII art. 13 cyber regulation still pending).. Not reached: Acta Apostolicae Sedis issue-by-issue search (not needed: Governorate legislation listing used); ASIF website not browsed directly (web search only). Could not verify: Appointment of the Governorate's AI Commission (art. 14 DCCII): reported outside official sources only.; Publication of DCCII in the AAS supplement (stated as intended by the decree; not checked).. strategy, procurement, cyber-security, standards, sandbox, index-readiness, drafts, international, historical: no material found.
